body:
Wondering if anyone had a chance to look at my patch above? When I upgraded from 1.7 to 1.8.0 and then from 1.8.0 to 1.8.1, on both occasions I had to fix the code manually. So it would be great if the issue is fixed permanently so that the date range sliders will work.

If the proper way is to fork and do a pull request, let me know.

Workaround: Add  value (anything, anything) to the slider. The value will be ignored and the slider will behave properly.
```
if "test" not in streamlit.session_state:
    streamlit.session_state["test"] = (0.25, 0.75)
streamlit.slider("Test", min_value=0.0, max_value=1.0, key="test", value=(0.0, 0.0), on_change=lambda: print(streamlit.session_state))
```

Thanks @clo-vis for the suggestion!

Unfortunately that triggers a warning: "The widget with key "test" was created with a default value but also had its value set via the Session State API."

If setting the default value via Session State, it seems we cannot set it via "value" again because of this [line](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d71a6ac8c239f2a9be92d7c2ce9d2d4d93165db9/lib/streamlit/elements/slider.py#L187).

The warning is triggered only once (then _shown_default_value_warning is set to False and the warning is not shown anymore), so I open the page myself whenever I deploy the app and the users who use the page after me don't see the warning again.

Hi @crxi! 👋🏼 
Thank you for your submission and for seeking out a potential solution as well 😃 
If possible, we would sincerely appreciate you forking & posting a pull request so we can review/examine fix options.

## 📚 Context

Currently st.slider handles both range and single value sliders. 
Problem is happening when range value set from `session_state`. The problem is that by default since we have not read a value from session_state during creation, a single slider initiates, which then leads to incorrect behavior. 

The solution here (based on an idea from at #4648 ) is to access session_state, inspect is there a default value set from session_state, and if so, use that value during initialization.
